hardware.variant: One assembled kit with operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2.

inputs.name: Static FFS RAM root with console tools

scenario: Boot the parser-bridge Wi-Fi kernel and RAM root, bring up espwifi0, and run one active 2.4 GHz scan. Do not associate to any access point.
expected: The selected WPA/RSN parser completes without callback errors and returned metadata distinguishes protected network modes sufficiently to assess WPA3 and PMF.
observed: espwifi0 attached and was brought up. The one scan command returned 14 and then 16 records; these are result polls, not a unique-network or BSS count. No WPA/RSN parser callback errors appeared. Reported auth enums included 3 and 4; the selected ESP-IDF 6.1 header defines 3 as WPA2-PSK and 4 as WPA/WPA2-PSK. The captured scan output contains neither BSSID nor raw RSN AKM/PMF fields, so actual security modes and unique BSS count cannot be established. The shell remained responsive; no association, authentication or DHCP was tested.
limits: One operator-reported V1.2 sample and one RAM-only boot; this does not establish another board revision or persistent installation.

Selected ESP-IDF 6.1 defines auth enum 3 as WPA2-PSK, 4 as WPA/WPA2-PSK, 7 as WPA3-PSK, and 8 as WPA2/WPA3-PSK mixed mode. The scan reported enums 3 and 4; these values alone do not establish the AP security modes.
The captured scan output provides no BSSID, raw RSN AKM or PMF fields. Unique BSS count and actual WPA3/PMF classification therefore remain unknown.
No association, authentication, DHCP, roaming or sustained transfer was tested.
